correctness.rationale: For a cyclic quasi-hereditary Nakayama algebra, a simple module of projective dimension 2 forces a plateau in the lifted Kupisch endpoints rho_i=i+c_i. Periodicity bounds both plateau parameters by n, so all projective and injective lengths are at most 2n-1. Long injectives have a common top, and the uniserial Hom formula shows that at most one injective-projective pair can contribute dimension 2; all other pairs contribute at most 1. The explicit Kupisch series (2,n+1,n,...,3) has every Hom pair nonzero and exactly one pair of dimension 2, giving n^2+1.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2020 MathOverflow post explicitly asks for this maximum and conjectures n^2+1, and the accessible page remains unanswered. Uematsu-Yamagata and Marczinzik-Sen provide quasi-hereditary Nakayama criteria but not this Frobenius-dimension theorem. The full July 2026 preprint Bounds on Frobenius dimension was inspected and contains no Nakayama, quasi-hereditary, or serial specialization. Targeted synonymous searches did not locate the n^2+1 theorem or the unique-double-Hom mechanism.

value.rationale: The theorem settles an explicit 2020 extremal problem for every n>=2, supplies a uniform sharp family, and explains the simple extremal formula through a structural restriction on Hom spaces between indecomposable injectives and projectives.
